section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the discourse to a maamar by the Baal HaHilula on "Ashrei Yosheivei Beisecha," explaining that Ashrei refers to the Kesser Elyon, called Oneg (delight), which clothes itself in Abba and Imma, called "Yosheivei Beisecha."
section.t: And one should connect this with the discourse of the Baal HaHilula
(which has not yet been printed)
beginning with the words "Ashrei Yosheivei Beisecha"7
[And it seems that the discourse beginning with these words in the Siddur of the Mitteler Rebbe
is based on the aforementioned discourse,
and it is explained at greater length in the commentary on the words by the Mitteler Rebbe8,
and in the commentary on the words by the Tzemach Tzedek9
– with the addition of notes and cross-references],
which explains10
there the entire prayer of Ashrei until the verse "Hashem is close to all who call upon Him,"
(and the continuation of the verses has already been explained in other places in the discourses of the Alter Rebbe).
And the content of its explanation is,
that Ashrei is the aspect of Kesser Elyon,
which is called Ashrei, which is the matter of delight
(from the phrase "In my Ashrei, for the daughters call me fortunate"11).
And likewise, Kesser Elyon is called Atik, which is the aspect of the supernal delight,
and from it, it clothes itself in Abba and Imma, who are called "Yosheivei Beisecha,"
which are the two houses of Chochmah and Binah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the psalm "Tehillah L'Dovid," where "Aromimcha" refers to Kesser, which is elevated above all Sefiros, and its revelation comes through Malchus, which descends to clarify sparks, requiring protection from the innermost aspect of Kesser.
section.t: And he continues to explain the psalm12
"Tehillah L'Dovid, Aromimcha Elokai HaMelech etc."
(And this psalm is the essence of the prayer of Ashrei and is the reason for its recitation,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said13
"One who recites 'Tehillah L'Dovid' three times daily is guaranteed etc.").
And he explains regarding this,
that "Aromimcha" is also an aspect of Kesser,
which is called "Ram" because it is elevated above all ten Sefiros,
for all ten Sefiros are in a state of revelation,
but Kesser is the concealment of all concealments,
and therefore he said regarding Kesser "Aromimcha,"
meaning "I will exalt You."
And this is also the explanation of "Aromimcha" with a Chaf,
for the Chaf also alludes to the aspect of Kesser,
first, because Chaf is the beginning of the word Kesser,
and second, because Chaf is twice Yud,
which is ten Sefiros in direct light from above to below,
and ten Sefiros in returning light from below to above14,
and they are included in Kesser
[unlike when they are by themselves, it is not possible for them to be in the number twenty,
for they are two different categories15,
and specifically in Kesser they are included as one entity of twenty].
However,
the fact that it says "Aromimcha" in the second person,
seemingly implies that it is an expression of revelation,
yet Kesser is hidden from the comprehension of created beings.
But regarding this, it says afterwards "Elokai HaMelech,"
meaning,
the main reason for the ability to comprehend it is because it clothes itself in the King,
that is, Malchus of Atzilus,
in which Kesser clothes itself,
for the end is interwoven in the beginning etc.16
And the reason is,
because when Malchus of Atzilus descends very low to the place of the kelipos to clarify sparks,
for this reason the kelipos are able to draw sustenance from it,
and therefore it needs protection from a high place,
that is, from the aspect of the light of Kesser,
and within this itself,
not only the externality of Kesser,
but also the internality of Kesser,
and as above, that Ashrei refers to Atik, which is the supernal delight, that is, the internality of Kesser
(and not only Will, which is the externality of Kesser),
and this aspect, which is very high,
is drawn and interwoven specifically in Malchus, which is the last of the Sefiros.
And it can be said that this is also the meaning of "Aromimcha" with an elongated Chaf,
as is known, that the extension of the Chaf below the line indicates that it descends very, very low.
And this is what continues "and I will bless Your name forever and ever,"
that after the illumination of Kesser is revealed in Malchus,
then influence will be drawn from it to the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,
and this is "and I will bless" from the language of "one who layers a vine"17,
that is, the drawing down that is drawn from the aspect of Malchus, which is called "Your name,"
which is an aspect of name and illumination only
(and not essence),
and the drawing down is "forever and ever,"
meaning that the drawing down to Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah is without end,
so that it can give life to creations without end,
even though this is from the aspect of "Your name" alone.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the continuation of the psalm, where "Poseach Es Yadecha" refers to the opening of the Yud's of the Tikkunei Dikna, drawing Kesser through Yesod, and "Karov Hashem" indicates that Ein Sof is equally invested in Asiyah as in Atzilus.
section.t: And similarly, it is explained in the continuation of the discourse near its end18,
regarding what is stated in the continuation of the psalm,
"You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor, righteous is Hashem etc., Hashem is close etc."
And he explains this based on what our sages, of blessed memory, said19
"Do not read 'Yadecha' (Your hand) but rather 'Yudecha' (Your Yuds),"
and he explains that "You open Your hand" means the opening of the Yuds of the Tikkunei Dikna,
that the Tikkunei Dikna are Yuds and Vavs that are drawn and opened in Chochmah,
and this is the matter of the drawing down of Kesser.
And this drawing down is in a manner of "and satisfies every living thing with favor,"
meaning,
that Yesod is called "Chai" (living),
because through it come all the influences,
and therefore Kesser is drawn down into the aspect of Yesod so that through it, influence can flow to the entire order of Hishtalshelus.
And he continues to explain20
what is said "Righteous is Hashem in all His ways,"
that "Tzaddik" (righteous) is also Yesod,
and the difference between when it is called "Chai" and when it is called "Tzaddik" is,
that when it influences vitality to the internality of the worlds, it is called "Chai,"
and when it influences vitality to the externality of the worlds, it is called "Tzaddik,"
and this is "Righteous is Hashem in all His ways,"
that this drawing down is then drawn into the aspect of the externality of the worlds,
until "in all His ways,"
in all the ways of the order of Hishtalshelus.
And he continues to explain21
what is said "Hashem is close to all who call upon Him,"
that this is because Ein Sof is invested in Asiyah just as in Atzilus,
and therefore "Hashem is close to all who call upon Him" equally.
